newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha easier in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha easier in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices drifted lower on Thursday in a market devoid of active traders, market participants said.
The naphtha market was quiet as players in Singapore were already in a holiday mood ahead of the extended weekend, they said.
Bids for first-half June open-spec naphtha were heard at $223.50, with offers at $223.75. It was sold by a western trading house to a Singapore trader at $225.00 on Wednesday.
Also on Wednesday, second-half June was bought by a South Korean trader at $223.50.
In middle distillates, high domestic stocks put downward pressure on Japan's gas oil imports, traders said.

Oil firms in Japan, which usually start seeking spot gas oil cargoes at the end of March or early April to meet seasonal upturn in domestic demand, have yet to begin scouting the market earnestly this year, they said.
Gas oil inventories at the end of February totalled 2.34 million kilolitres, an increase of 39 percent from a year ago.
Levels for spot kerosene cargoes were notionally assessed at $1.30 to 1.50 over the mean of Singapore quotes.
